title: Montreal Victoire, Team Canada star Marie-Philip Poulin to undergo knee surgery
content:
Marie-Philip Poulin, captain of the Montreal Victoire and the Canadian women’s national hockey team, will undergo surgery on her ACL and meniscus in July and will be out for an undetermined amount of time.

Poulin, 35, fought back tears as she and Victoire general manager Danièle Sauvageau announced the update during a virtual news conference Thursday.

Poulin initially injured her right knee during the Olympics in February but eventually returned to the lineup, scoring twice in Canada’s semifinal win over Switzerland. She missed the Victoire’s first game after the tournament but said she was “feeling good” when she returned to the PWHL in March.

However, Poulin was hurt in her third game back on March 15, tearing her ACL and meniscus. She missed 10 of the Victoire’s final 11 regular-season games before playing through pain to tie for the team lead with 8 playoff points and help Montreal win its first Walter Cup championship. Poulin was named playoff MVP.

“I played the best I could with a torn ACL and meniscus because I wanted to be part of this journey that led us to hoist the Walter Cup,” Poulin said in a statement released by the team Thursday. “It was with this goal in mind that I worked tirelessly to return to the game this season.

“It has become clear that if I want to continue playing at a high level, surgery is necessary.”

Throughout Montreal’s playoff run, Poulin’s teammates and coach Kori Cheverie alluded to the physical pain Poulin was battling. She scored two game winners in Montreal’s semifinal series against the Minnesota Frost and set up the game winners in games 2 and 4 against the Ottawa Charge in the finals. TV cameras frequently caught her wincing on the bench.

“I don’t think there’s any words to describe Marie to start with and what she decided following this injury,” Sauvageau said Thursday. “Watching her say: ‘I’m going to do this rehab. I’m going to do everything I possibly can to come back,’ was unbelievable.”

When asked whether the injury would cause Poulin to miss the entire 2026-27 season, Sauvageau didn’t go into specifics. She said they would “take the time to re-evaluate” and make the “best decision.”

The typical timeline for recovery from a torn ACL is around nine to 12 months. Poulin said in French that retirement hadn’t crossed her mind and that she will do everything she can to come back.

“I’m going to focus all my energy on my recovery once the surgery is done so that I can return to the game in the best physical form possible,” she said.

Poulin will almost certainly miss the world championships in November, Canada’s first since the post-Olympics departure of general manager Gina Kingsbury and coach Troy Ryan. The roster is expected to feature several other major changes: Center Blayre Turnbull announced Monday that she is pregnant with her first child and is due in December, and a youth movement could replace other key veterans.

As for the Victoire, Sauvageau was forced to watch defenders Erin Ambrose, Julia Gosling and Amanda Boulier land elsewhere during the expansion process, but she added free-agent forwards Emma Maltais and Jessie Eldridge and PWHL Draft pick Petra Nieminen. Now their task is to repeat as champions despite probably missing a player whose skill and leadership are largely irreplaceable.
